title: TrackRef
description:
A visual track, scoped to exactly one stream and one wall-clock UTC hour. This is the `vision` domain's substitute for a subject reference: vision carries no `subject_ref`, because a pseudonym is only obtainable if the producer can ask the gateway who a person is, and it can only ask if it holds a persistent biometric template - which is the root identifier under another name, accumulating in the one domain the pseudonymisation construction exists to keep it out of.

`track_id` is a random 64-bit value. It MUST NOT be reused, MUST NOT be shared between streams, and MUST NOT cross the window boundary. A person walking through 14:59:59 into 15:00:00 receives two unrelated tracks. That truncation is the bound, not a defect: a rolling one-hour lifetime would track better and prove less, and any analysis needing continuity across the seam is an analysis this system declines to support.

Banned in `analytical` retention - an hour-scoped per-person handle in a 90-day store reconstructs exactly what the scoping prevents. Permitted in `evidential`, which `footage-sealed` requires.

stream_id.description: Registered stream the track belongs to. A track is meaningless outside it.

track_id.description: Random 64-bit track identifier, lowercase hex. Never reused, never carried across a window.

window.description: Wall-clock UTC hour bucket the track lives in, e.g. "2026-09-07T14Z".
